output.scope_note: The paper is a simulation methods study of Li+ conduction in PEO/LiTFSI, a solid-state polymer electrolyte, and reports MD-computed ionic conductivities for it; the toy model is not a real material and is excluded.

records.material_as_written: PEO/LiTFSI (200 (PEO)9 chains with 150 LiTFSI, r = 1/12 Li+/EO), Nernst-Einstein conductivity
records.evidence_quote: The Nernst-Einstein approach spectacularly overestimates the conductivity by a factor of 10 (σNE = 9.0 · 10−3 S/cm, σE = 8.8 · 10−4 S/cm).
records.notes: Simulated PEO/LiTFSI at r = 1/12 Li+/EO; the paper states a target temperature of 363 K for the configurations (90 °C conversion is arithmetic). Not an experimental value. Conductivity from Nernst-Einstein approximation, not Einstein form.

records.material_as_written: PEO/LiTFSI (200 (PEO)9 chains with 150 LiTFSI, r = 1/12 Li+/EO), Einstein conductivity
records.measurement_method: MD simulation (Einstein form, lag-time limit of collective MSD)
records.evidence_quote: The Nernst-Einstein approach spectacularly overestimates the conductivity by a factor of 10 (σNE = 9.0 · 10−3 S/cm, σE = 8.8 · 10−4 S/cm).
records.notes: Reference Einstein conductivity from MD of PEO/LiTFSI; paper notes it may not be fully converged even after 100 ns. Temperature 363 K is the target temperature of the MD runs.
